stories.title: Mangione pleads guilty to federal charges in UnitedHealthcare CEO killing
new_facts: Mangione pleaded guilty (past tense confirmed); admitted to following then shooting Thompson.
Defense attorney Karen Friedman Agnifilo spoke to reporters outside federal court after plea.
Mangione read a statement in court describing targeting Thompson outside an investor conference.
Mangione told judge: 'I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan. I knew what I was doing was illegal.'
Mangione's age given as 28 (ledger had 26); hearing described as hastily scheduled.
Mangione told judge he 'shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan in the back' with stated intent.
Mangione quoted: 'I shot Mr Thompson and he died.' Thompson's age given as 50.
Plea deal raises double jeopardy concern for future of Mangione's New York state trial.
stories.line: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to federal stalking charges in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, leaving his state trial status unclear.

stories.title: Bezos-backed group buys controlling stake option in Liverpool FC
new_facts: Bezos-led group buys minority stake in Liverpool FC with option to become majority owner within a year.
Consortium includes ex-QPR owner Amit Bhatia; deal worth £1.65bn; FSG also owns Boston Red Sox.
30% stake sold; Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin also in consortium; Bhatia becomes vice-chairman; club valued at £5.5bn.
Consortium led by son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal; valuation stated as over $7bn.
stories.line: Jeff Bezos and partners acquire 30% of Liverpool FC with an option to take full control later.

new_facts: Google now lets users remove visible watermarks from AI-generated images; invisible watermarks remain.
Judge gives Google one week to fix anticompetitive app store download behavior in Google Play.
stories.line: Google removes watermarks from AI-generated images and faces a court order to change Play Store practices.

stories.title: Stephen Bear jailed for sex offender register breach
new_facts: Stephen Bear jailed for breaching sex offender register; taunted police from Brazil beach.
Bear sentenced to 24 weeks in prison for sex offender register breach; also separately jailed for restraining order breach.
stories.line: TV personality Stephen Bear sentenced to jail for violating sex offender register requirements while evading authorities abroad.

stories.title: American missionary freed after nine months in Niger captivity
new_facts: Kevin Rideout freed after October kidnapping in Niger; in good health with U.S. officials.
Entirely different story: wife of U.S. soldier released from federal immigration custody after a month detained.
Rideout was kidnapped 150 feet from Niger's presidential palace in Niamey.
SIM International named as Rideout's organization; family reunion imminent.
stories.line: American missionary Kevin Rideout freed after nine months of captivity in Niger following kidnapping in October.

stories.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s, citing free speech
new_facts: France's top court blocked a social media ban for under-15s, citing freedom of expression; Macron ordered rewrite.
stories.line: France's constitutional court blocked a proposed ban on social media for children under 15, ruling it violated freedom of expression.

stories.title: Farage wins Clacton by-election as watchdog reopens party donation inquiry
new_facts: Electoral watchdog has reopened investigation into Farage's £5m gift after election win.
Count Binface's alter ego is comedian Jon Harvey; CBS frames result as his greatest success yet.
Count Binface (Jon Harvey) will perform at the Edinburgh Fringe after the by-election.
Farage cancelled a major speech planned for the morning after his by-election victory.
Count Binface finished second in the Clacton by-election.
Farage won with 62.8% of the vote; donor named as Christopher Harborne; donation figure is £5 million; Farage missed the count citing a threat.
Farage called the by-election explicitly in protest at parliamentary and media scrutiny of his finances.
Only two of 34 candidates secured enough votes to reclaim their deposit; one candidate got seven votes.
stories.line: Nigel Farage wins a UK by-election in Clacton; a watchdog reopens an investigation into a £5m donation to his party.

stories.title: Woman charged with felonies in World War II Memorial vandalism
new_facts: Woman charged over vandalism; DOJ involved; paint described as red and green.
Woman arrested and faces two felony charges; top federal prosecutor in DC announced.
Trump publicly reacted to the vandalism, expressing upset.
Pirro (named prosecutor) announced the arrest and two felony charges.
Suspect identified as Melissa L. Farris; faces up to 10 years in prison.
Trump called vandals "animals" on record.
Interior Department called incident "utter disgrace"; uniformed police and National Guard responded.
stories.line: A woman was arrested and charged with felonies for vandalizing the World War II Memorial in Washington with graffiti and bubbles.

stories.title: Trump seeks Supreme Court approval to continue White House ballroom work
new_facts: Trump cites Turkey catering truck escape as national security justification in SCOTUS ballroom filing.
Deputy national security adviser Andy Baker plans to leave his post in coming weeks.
Trump asked Supreme Court to allow White House ballroom construction to continue after lower court blocked it.
stories.line: Trump petitions Supreme Court to continue White House ballroom construction while legal challenge proceeds.
